title: orient returns hard MCP error (-32602) on unindexed workspace instead of a hint
description:
On an unindexed workspace orient throws a hard protocol error rather than a structured, recoverable response. Compare the soft-error path orient already uses for unresolved scope (returns {error, hint} with is_error=false). An unindexed workspace should degrade the same way: a soft result naming the workspace and pointing at `sutra_workspace(path=...)` / add-root, not a red -32602.

Note: this failure mode is shared by other sutra tools on unindexed workspaces, but orient is where it bites (it's what agents reach for on a fresh repo). Consider fixing at the shared entry point.

GATED on sutra/312: if orient is deleted, re-scope to the shared tool entry point or close wontfix.
reproduction: Call sutra_orient on a workspace sutra hasn't indexed (history: manas-brain, colibri) → `MCP error -32602: [workspaces] not found: workspace '...'. List workspaces with 'sutra workspaces list'`. 2 of 7 historical calls. This is the "goes red" Josh sees.

messages.author: user
messages.text: wontfix — superseded by sutra/312 (delete orient). Caveat: the hard MCP -32602 on an unindexed workspace is SHARED across sutra tools, not orient-specific — deleting orient does not fix it elsewhere, it just removes the surface where it was most often hit. Not re-filing unbidden. If the unindexed→red UX is worth softening generally (structured {error,hint} pointing at sutra_workspace(path=) instead of a protocol error), file a fresh task against the shared tool dispatch entry point.
